note: FIRST SOCO KEEPER, REGISTERED 2026-09-16 (lane SOCO-40). There is no predecessor — this is the first SOCO solve of any kind, so nothing is superseded and rule 35 [R-PROMOTE] has nothing to prune. DETERMINATION NOT-YET (rubric v3.8, PRICE UNSCORED), and it is the keeper anyway under rule 1 [R-STRUCT]: it is the most structurally faithful SOCO run that exists, and a determination is not a promotion test. THE DEFINING CONSTRAINT: SOCO HAS NO PRICE BENCHMARK AND NEVER WILL. Its footprint publishes no LMP, hub or clearing price, so data/raw/_validation-source/actual_lmp.json carries NO SOCO block and MUST NOT GAIN ONE — a placeholder would break calibration_verdict._price_reference_absent and silently move SOCO onto the ordinary determination path. C3a / C3b / C3c are UNSCORABLE, NOT FAILED. The ceiling is PHYSICALLY-CALIBRATED (PRICE UNSCORED) and SOCO can NEVER read CALIBRATED. Gate G17 stands absolutely: no neighbouring hub, no proxy, no cost-stack price, ever. The model's own load-weighted mean LMP (33.32 / 31.14 / 199.34 $/MWh) is MODEL-ONLY and UNVERIFIED and is never quoted as price skill. THE RECIPE: the CLI's all-defaults ISO-agnostic backcast construction, 28 non-default ScenarioConfig fields, no --set and no --offer-curve-json, on three geographic zones (SOCO_AL / SOCO_GA / SOCO_MS) over measured FERC-714 shares from the FIVE fully-cited respondents, Tier-3 documented non-binding links (24,400 / 4,300 MW, both measured at dual 0.000), served measured EIA-930 interchange, VOLL 61,900. EVERY offer_curve_by_group BAND IS EXACTLY 1.0 on all 13 groups, offer_curve_overrides and offer_curve_deltas are null, and authorized_price_tuning is declared NONE — the rule 1 [R-STRUCT] authorized channel is not merely unused but unreachable here, since with no price benchmark there is no residual to tune against. There is no soco.py offer-curve delta module; SOCO rides the pure ISO-agnostic GENERIC_BASE_OFFER_CURVE, so rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]'s neutral-fallback requirement holds by construction. THE OWNER'S COAL-SPLIT INSTRUCTION IS WHAT THIS KEEPER EXECUTES, verbatim: "Coal should be split into types. Completely eliminate the single coal class." Done zero-LP by scripts/data/derive_coal_supply.py --iso SOCO --census-vintage 2023 2024 2025, which wrote six rows to data/raw/_processed-legacy/coal_supply_SOCO.csv (Barry 3 / Gaston 26 / Bowen 703 bituminous; Miller 6002 / Daniel 6073 / Scherer 6257 prb) — every SOCO coal plant resolves, COAL_BIT 5,150.5 MW and COAL_PRB 6,361.5 MW measured on the fleet, bare COAL 0.0 MW. Machine-verified on all three class_hourly parquets: every year carries COAL_BIT and COAL_PRB and NO bare COAL. It is a RECLASSIFICATION, not a re-dispatch — every non-coal class is byte-identical to the unsplit arm, the two coal classes sum to the unsplit COAL to the GWh (33.142 / 34.676 / 47.662), and the 2023 and 2024 P0 objectives are identical to the cent (3690944814.1196 / 3398767416.6013); only 2025's moves (5682126660.3872 -> 5680277825.0155), in the scarcity hours its hydro hole creates. WHAT IT BOUGHT: C1's failing rows fall from SEVEN to ONE. Every coal row now passes, because the benchmark scores coal on EIA-923 fuel codes and the model was previously offering one blended class against two benchmark rows (the SPP-40 §7.3 defect) — 2024 COAL_BIT now lands at 12.256 TWh against 12.257 actual. THE GATES: C1 FAIL (1 row of 14; C1 all 13/14, free 9/10), C2 PASS, C4 PASS, C6 PASS, C8 PASS; C3a / C3b / C3c SKIPPED-UNSCORABLE; C5a is REPORTED-ONLY (-5.3 / -8.9 / +4.9 %) and contributes no status. grade_summary 4 of 5 scored, 1 fail, 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats. The LP sends energy to combustion turbines that the real system sent to gas steam units. C2 / C4 / C6 / C8 still PASS, C3a/b/c still UNSCORABLE, 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats, determination NOT-YET both ways. The owner ruled that a structural gain with a gate regression may still be a keeper, and this is that trade taken deliberately. WHAT THE LANE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, and it outlives the arm: the CT_PEAKER/ST_GAS misallocation is NOT a cost-side defect at all. (a) Every offer_curve_by_group band is the identity 1.0, so each SOCO class is a SINGLE FLAT PRICE BLOCK -- confirmed in the committed class_band_hourly sidecar, where 2023 ST_GAS ran 1.117 / 1.138 / 1.141 / 0.600 TWh across the four bands, flat -- so every curve-SHAPED lever is provably inert for SOCO by construction and SOCO's only available levers are PHYSICS and DATA levers. (b) The MEASURED separation between the classes is +0.713 MMBtu/MWh (CT 10.911 vs ST 10.198, CAMPD loaded hours) while the MODEL already separates them by +1.983 -- 2.8x -- and CT_PEAKER still over-ran by 8.221 TWh, so no admissible cost-side change closes a gap the model is already overshooting. (c) The real separation is COMMITMENT: at UNIT grain SOCO gas boilers run 94-144 h campaigns and start ~9-11 times a year while combustion turbines run 8-9 h blocks and start ~57-60 times a year, and the model gives BOTH classes min_run_hours = 0 and min_down_hours = 0 while the CT_PEAKER econ and peak tranches -- holding 10.9 of the class's 12.755 TWh in 2023 -- carry ZERO startup cost. TWO CELLS WERE ADJUDICATED WITHOUT SPENDING A SPAN: gas_commitment_bridge -> R (of 386 boiler downtime gaps, 68.7 % exceed 72 h and account for 169,303 of 171,734 gap-hours = 98.6 %; only 150 unit-hours across three years fall inside the 8 h ST_GAS min-down -- SOCO's boilers do not two-shift, so the bridge is INERT BY MEASUREMENT) and tranche_startup_amortization -> G with NO reopen condition (it is the FERC Order-825 fast-start PRICING object, bid markup only, and SOCO has no clearing price -- derived from SOCO's own market design, not transferred from CAISO's G, per rule 28(d)). THE A/B IS CLEAN AND THAT IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: all EIGHT shared_inputs content hashes are IDENTICAL between this keeper and the one it supersedes (eia923-c6e433cd9eb4, eia930-af1df2c6e425, campd-eecf72fbab56 and the five unit_outages*), and the shared store rebuilt locally via --rebuild-benchmark (NO re-solve) reproduced the same three hashes. SOCO's bench parts were DELIBERATELY NOT rebuilt: check_bench_freshness is red on 44 of 44 parts across EVERY ISO from commit ed96378e (caiso-284) editing scripts/render_calibration_html.py, a PAYLOAD_SOURCE; this lane touched no fingerprint source, and rebuilding SOCO's bench would have scored the arm against a different benchmark from its control and destroyed the rule 29(b) form-4 comparison. A RULE-24 [R-REGISTRY] GAP WAS REPAIRED EN ROUTE: measured_ct_heat_rates was registered, cache-key-registered, carried True by FIVE ISOs' keepers (CAISO/MISO/NEISO/NYISO/PJM) -- and had NO CLI flag in run_calibration_full.py, the orchestrator every keeper is solved with, so it was unreachable for SOCO, NWPP and SPP. Wired along the identical eight-site path egrid_identity_heat_rates takes, BooleanOptionalAction / default None, so unset is byte-identical for every other ISO and every existing keeper; check_cache_key_registration passes. WHAT THIS KEEPER DOES NOT FIX, stated at the gate rather than absorbed: the eGRID plant-blend defect reaches FAR beyond CT_PEAKER and this keeper repairs only the CT slice. 11,777 MW -- 26.0 % of SOCO's thermal capacity -- sits at NINE multi-technology plants, and at EIGHT of them EVERY unit carries a SINGLE blended heat rate: Barry (3) prices 1,118.5 MW of coal + 1,821.2 MW of gas CC + 160.0 MW of gas steam all at 8.994965; Victor J Daniel Jr (6073) prices 1,004.0 MW of coal + 1,132.4 MW of gas CC all at 8.399, which no coal unit can physically attain; E C Gaston (26) prices coal, gas steam and oil all at 11.551. Every offer_curve_by_group band is still EXACTLY 1.0 on all 13 groups, authorized_price_tuning is declared NONE (unreachable in principle -- with no price benchmark there is no residual to tune), and the DOF ledger is UNCHANGED at n_entries 3 / n_residual 1: this lane added ZERO free parameters. WHY IT IS THE KEEPER -- rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] and rule 1 [R-STRUCT], never the residual. eGRID joins heat rate at PLANT grain (PLNT23.PLHTRT), so every generator at a multi-technology plant inherits one generation-weighted blend: Victor J Daniel Jr (6073) priced 1,004.0 MW of coal at 8.399 MMBtu/MWh -- which NO coal boiler can physically attain, its own meter reading 12.895 -- and Barry (3) priced 1,118.5 MW of coal + 1,821.2 MW of gas CC + 160.0 MW of gas steam all at 8.994965. The construction is each prime-mover family's own sum(UNT23.HTIAN)/sum(GEN23.GENNTAN) from the SAME eGRID vintage the plant-grain join reads: a finer read of the identical source on the identical boundary, zero degrees of freedom. It moves 24 generator rows / 6,473.2 MW at FOUR plants (Barry 3, Greene County 10, Jack Watson 2049, Victor J Daniel Jr 6073). THIS LANE REPAIRED THE MECHANISM'S CONSTRUCTION BEFORE ARMING IT, and that is the lane's real product. The derive's central claim -- that the family rate replaces the blend on the identical net-annual boundary -- is an IDENTITY (sum HTIAN / sum GENNTAN == PLHTRT) and is now CHECKED. Over SOCO's nine covered plants it partitions them with three orders of magnitude to spare: FOUR recompose at ratio 1.000 and FIVE at 4.05-8.40. The five are cogeneration paper mills, where eGRID STEAM-CREDITS PLHTIAN and does NOT steam-credit the unit sheet's HTIAN, so a family rate there charges the host's process steam to the electric output (Pensacola Florida Plant recomposes to 22.537 against a published 5.568). The pre-existing out_of_window guard is a per-FAMILY plausibility test and caught ONLY the steam halves; the TURBINE halves landed INSIDE 3,000-30,000 Btu/kWh and WERE BEING APPLIED -- four rows, 160.0 MW, onto CT_CHP and CC_CHP, the latter a scored C1 row. That is rule 14's misalignment exception verbatim, so a per-PLANT boundary_mismatch flag now refuses them and SOCO's artifact goes 12 applied -> 8. The guard is DERIVE-SIDE, never consumer-side: a guard inside _apply_egrid_family_heat_rates is default-on and would have moved CAISO's keeper fleet from this lane (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]). NO src/market_sim FILE IS TOUCHED. BOUNDARY_IDENTITY_TOL = 0.005 is a rounding allowance incapable of being tuned: over all 26 covered plants in the three ISOs carrying an artifact the passing side sits at 1.0000 and the failing side starts at 2.800, so every value in (0.001, 1.8) gives the identical partition. Declared ex ante and never swept. RULE 19 [R-ONE-MECH], MACHINE-VERIFIED: precedence is structural, not declared. The family rate is applied at FRAME level in _rows_to_generators; measured_ct_heat_rates is applied inside the ROW LOOP gated on group == 'CT_PEAKER'. So measured CAMPD > eGRID family > eGRID plant blend, and CT_PEAKER's cap-weighted heat rate is BYTE-IDENTICAL at 11.2666 on both sides -- Greene County's computed GT family rate (14.105) and Watson's (21.925) are both entirely overwritten. Nothing is priced twice. CC_CHP / CT_CHP / ST_CHP heat rates are byte-identical too, by the boundary guard. THE GATES ARE FLAT, WHICH IS A STRONGER CASE THAN THE OWNER'S STANDARD REQUIRED: C1 all 12/14 and free 8/10 on BOTH sides, the SAME two rows fail (2023 CT_PEAKER, 2023 ST_GAS), C2/C4/C6/C8 PASS on both, 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats on both, grade_summary identical, and NO row changes status in either direction. C5a is REPORTED-ONLY and contributes no status (2024 -9.0% -> -10.0%). THE EFFECT WAS PREDICTED BEFORE THE SOLVE AND CONFIRMED, INCLUDING THE PART THAT IS UNFLATTERING: PRECOMMIT section 2.2 registered that coal would fall, CC_REGULAR would rise, and that CT_PEAKER and ST_GAS would NOT materially improve -- so THIS ARM DOES NOT FIX SOCO'S HEADLINE DEFECT, and the PRECOMMIT said so rather than the FINDING saying it afterwards.
